Name: Scalpel
Description: A small and extremely sharp bladed instrument used for surgery, anatomical dissection. Scalpels may be single-use disposable or re-usable.
KeyFeatures: Handle can be reusable with disposable blades.
Used for making initial incisions and cutting tissue.

Name: Straight Mayo Scissor
Description: A type of surgical scissor, often used for cutting sutures (hence the common nickname 'suture scissors'). They are also used for cutting heavy tissues like fascia.
KeyFeatures: Heavy scissors with straight, semi-blunt blades.
Ideal for cutting surface-level tissues and sutures.
Less common for deep tissue dissection.

Name: Curved Mayo Scissor
Description: Used to cut thick tissues such as those found in the uterus, muscles, breast, and foot. The curved design allows for deeper penetration into the wound.
KeyFeatures: Curved blades that match the contour of the body.
Allows for better visualization and precision in deep wounds.
Heavier than most scissors for cutting tough tissue.

Name: Metzenbaum Scissors
Description: Surgical scissors designed for cutting delicate tissue and blunt dissection. The scissors come in variable lengths and have a relatively long shank-to-blade ratio.
KeyFeatures: Long shanks and short, delicate blades.
Used for fine dissection and cutting of soft tissues.
